b: Aditi Anand is an illustrator, author and printmaker from India. In 2024, she graduated with distinction from the MA in Children’s Book Illustration at the Cambridge School of Art, UK. Aditi has worked with Penguin…
f: Aditi Anand is an illustrator, author and printmaker from India. In 2024, she graduated with distinction from the MA in Children’s Book Illustration at the Cambridge School of Art, UK. Aditi has worked with Penguin Random House India, Pratham Books and Walker Books UK. She has won several awards, including the V&A Illustration Award. Her work has been exhibited across India, the UK, Italy, China, and Australia, including at the British Council in India and the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.

b: Aditi Krishnakumar is a writer, mathematician-in-training and private consultant. She’s written seven books, including Codex: The Lost Treasure of the Indus, which won the Scholastic Asian Book Award and was nominated…
f: Aditi Krishnakumar is a writer, mathematician-in-training and private consultant. She’s written seven books, including Codex: The Lost Treasure of the Indus, which won the Scholastic Asian Book Award and was nominated for the Singapore Book Award. In addition to her work as a writer, Aditi has spent several years working in finance in India and Singapore. In her free time, Aditi enjoys reading, painting, and learning to play the piano. Delegate | 2025 | 2026

b: Alankrita Amaya is an award-winning children’s book author and illustrator who spends her days dreaming up whimsical worlds in her cozy home studio in Bangalore, where she lives with her husband and their cat. Her work…
f: Alankrita Amaya is an award-winning children’s book author and illustrator who spends her days dreaming up whimsical worlds in her cozy home studio in Bangalore, where she lives with her husband and their cat. Her work is inspired by the magic hidden in everyday life. Some of her acclaimed books include Little Laali, Muft Ki Kulfi and Boodabim. She is also the co-founder of Hallubol, an initiative that preserves local Dakhni culture through bilingual comics. When she’s not making books, Alankrita can be found talking to cats, making candles or tending to her garden. Delegate | 2025 | 2026

b: Allie Millington is the New York Times bestselling author of heartfelt books for the young and young at heart. Olivetti , her debut middle grade novel, was an instant national bestseller and received a glowing review in…
f: Allie Millington is the New York Times bestselling author of heartfelt books for the young and young at heart. Olivetti , her debut middle grade novel, was an instant national bestseller and received a glowing review in the New York Times by Tom Hanks. Her books have received several awards, been named on many state award reading lists, and listed as best books of the year by publications such as NPR, School Library Journal, The Boston Globe, and others. Allie’s latest book is When You Find A Question , and her next book, Trunk No.3 , is slated to release later this year. She lives near Atlanta with her family, their dog Crumpet, and a collection of clacking machines.

b: Amish Tripathi is an author, former diplomat, broadcaster, and cultural commentator. Since publishing his first book in 2010, he has written 12 bestselling books that have sold over 8 million copies and been translated…
f: Amish Tripathi is an author, former diplomat, broadcaster, and cultural commentator. Since publishing his first book in 2010, he has written 12 bestselling books that have sold over 8 million copies and been translated into 21 languages, making him the fastest-selling author in Indian publishing history. He has been regularly featured among Forbes India’s Top 100 Most Influential Celebrities. His recent honours include the Dwarka Prasad Agarwal Award (Jaipur Literature Festival 2024), Best Factual Presenter at the Asian Academy Creative Awards (2025), and an Honorary Doctorate from the University of York (2026). From 2019 to 2023, he served as Minister (Culture & Education) at the Indian High Commission to the UK and Director of The Nehru Centre, London. As a broadcaster, he has hosted acclaimed documentaries, including Journey of India and Ram Janmabhoomi – Return of a Splendid Sun. He is also co-creator of the upcoming AAA video game Age of Bhaarat.

b: Ananya Broker Parekh is a visual storyteller and illustrator whose work spans picture books, films, textiles, and newspapers. She has worked with The New York Times, The Guardian and the Museum of Broken Relationships,…
f: Ananya Broker Parekh is a visual storyteller and illustrator whose work spans picture books, films, textiles, and newspapers. She has worked with The New York Times, The Guardian and the Museum of Broken Relationships, among others. When she is not drawing, she goes for long walks, reads as many books as she can and thinks about what she’d like to make for dinner.

b: Angie Kang makes art in LA. She is the author/illustrator of OUR LAKE (Kokila) which received a Caldecott Honor, the Charlotte Zolotow Award, the Dilys Evans Founder’s Award, and was featured on “Best of” lists by NPR,…
f: Angie Kang makes art in LA. She is the author/illustrator of OUR LAKE (Kokila) which received a Caldecott Honor, the Charlotte Zolotow Award, the Dilys Evans Founder’s Award, and was featured on “Best of” lists by NPR, Publishers Weekly, Kirkus, School Library Journal, Horn Book, and more. She is also the illustrator of NAVIGATING NIGHT, written by Julie Leung (Anne Schwartz Books). Her work has appeared in The New Yorker, The Believer, Best Small Fictions, and elsewhere. She is a 2026 Sendak Fellow, the 2024 Ezra Jack Keats Fellow at MacDowell, and shortlisted for the 2023 Cartoonist Studio Prize. Find her at angiekang.net or on Instagram @anqiekanq.

b: Anna James is a writer and journalist from Northumberland. She is the author of the internationally bestselling children’s fantasy series Pages & Co , the #1 New York Times bestselling series The Chronicles of…
f: Anna James is a writer and journalist from Northumberland. She is the author of the internationally bestselling children’s fantasy series Pages & Co , the #1 New York Times bestselling series The Chronicles of Whetherwhy and Alice With a Why , the Blackwells Children’s Book of the Year in 2025. Formerly a school librarian and literary scout, Anna is also an arts journalist. She previously was Book News Editor at The Bookseller and Literary Editor for ELLE UK and now covers books and theatre on a freelance basis. She’s a regular chair for literary events, and is the co-curator and host of the LUSH Book Club. Anna hosts the Bookwandering podcast where she speaks with other creatives about their most beloved books for young people. She currently lives in north London with her husband. You can find her @acaseforbooks across social media.

b: Eager to tell stories that reveal our shared humanity and build empathy in a world yearning for solace, Arun Fulara is a writer and filmmaker based out of Mumbai. His short films have travelled internationally, winning…
f: Eager to tell stories that reveal our shared humanity and build empathy in a world yearning for solace, Arun Fulara is a writer and filmmaker based out of Mumbai. His short films have travelled internationally, winning multiple awards and acclaim. His fascination with the Himalayan valleys stems from childhood vacations spent travelling to his native village up in the hills. ‘Shera’, both the book and the film, are a product of that fascination and engagement with the Himalayan region.

b: Arundhati Venkatesh is the author of several bestselling and award-winning titles. Among her books is the bestselling Bookasura, which won the Comic Con 2015 Best Publication for Children Award, was shortlisted for the…
f: Arundhati Venkatesh is the author of several bestselling and award-winning titles. Among her books is the bestselling Bookasura, which won the Comic Con 2015 Best Publication for Children Award, was shortlisted for the Crossword Book Award 2016 and is on Amazon’s ‘100 Children’s Books to Read in a Lifetime’. Her middle-grade novel, Ramanujan: From Zero to Infinity, is bestselling as well and won the TokaBox Top South Asian Children’s Book Honor for 2022. Arundhati’s books in the Petu Pumpkin series – Tiffin Thief, Tooth Troubles and Cheater Peter – have been on Flipkart’s #1 and #3 positions for children, won the SCBWI Crystal Kite Award 2015 for India, Middle East and Asia, and been shortlisted for the the Neev Book Award 2019. Her three latest releases all happen to be hilarious books for ages 10+: PETU PUMPKIN: Freedom Fighter, RAMANUJAN: From Zero to Infinity, RAMAN & CHANDRASEKHAR: Lighting Up the Stars. b: Ashok Rajagopalan has been illustrating since 1989 and writing since 2006. He loves making up stories and drawing pictures that make people—especially little people—laugh. Readers may know him from the Gajapati Kulapati…
f: Ashok Rajagopalan has been illustrating since 1989 and writing since 2006. He loves making up stories and drawing pictures that make people—especially little people—laugh. Readers may know him from the Gajapati Kulapati books and the Adventures of Gulgul series, where elephants sneeze, kitch-hens cook, and surprises lurk around every corner. He enjoys reading, talking, laughing, and walking in the rain. On most days, he can be found doodling, staring out of windows, or wondering what his characters might do next. He lives in a green, quiet part of Chennai with his wonderfully noisy family, who provide plenty of stories, sounds, and laughter to keep his imagination busy.

b: Brogen Murphy graduated with a degree in Zoology from the University of Cambridge and then set about trying to figure out how best to save the world. They tried ecology field work, carbon offsetting and a brief stint in…
f: Brogen Murphy graduated with a degree in Zoology from the University of Cambridge and then set about trying to figure out how best to save the world. They tried ecology field work, carbon offsetting and a brief stint in climate activism, before spending fifteen years promoting clean technologies to help build a low-carbon future. When not writing, they can be found exploring the forest with their wife looking (down) for mushrooms or (up) for birds—and therefore often tripping over. Their debut novel Wildlands won the 2025 Children’s Wainwright Prize for Fiction.

b: Charbak Dipta is an Eisner-nominated graphic novelist and illustrator with more than 60 published books spanning India, the US, and beyond. A self-taught artist with over a decade of experience in graphic storytelling,…
f: Charbak Dipta is an Eisner-nominated graphic novelist and illustrator with more than 60 published books spanning India, the US, and beyond. A self-taught artist with over a decade of experience in graphic storytelling, he has exhibited his work at comic cons worldwide. Charbak holds an MA in Philosophy from Jadavpur University and is an alumnus of the University of Oxford.

b: Chatura Rao writes stories for children and long-form articles about the goings-on in the world. Her latest book is Leaf People, a novella about a brother, a sister, and a mysterious walking bush. Chatura’s older…
f: Chatura Rao writes stories for children and long-form articles about the goings-on in the world. Her latest book is Leaf People, a novella about a brother, a sister, and a mysterious walking bush. Chatura’s older picture books, Gone Grandmother and The Sweet Shop Wars, have won literary prizes. Her journalistic writing centres around community practices and gender, and has won regional and national awards. She is a visiting faculty at the Srishti-Manipal Institute of Art, Design and Technology. She served as the Children’s Honour Books curator at the Green Literature Festival 2025, and has enjoyed being the Festival Director of the Chandigarh Children’s Literature Festival since 2015. Chatura lives in a quiet suburb in Bangalore, occasionally leaving it to look for a new story or to help young people write their own original ones. She hopes everyone will spot magic in the ordinary long after they grow up! Delegate | 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 Making the Universal Personal

b: Christopher Myers is an artist and writer based in New York. He is widely acclaimed for his literary work for young people, as well as for his fine arts practices. Myers is interested in the aesthetic bridges that have…
f: Christopher Myers is an artist and writer based in New York. He is widely acclaimed for his literary work for young people, as well as for his fine arts practices. Myers is interested in the aesthetic bridges that have been built organically across cultures, classes, and geographies, and has lectured and exhibited his work internationally. Myers has curated shows in Vietnam; collaborated with traditional shadow puppet makers in Jogjakarta, young musicians in New Orleans, and weavers in Luxor. He has designed theater that has travelled from PS122 in New York City to the Genocide Memorial Theater in Kigali, Rwanda. He participated in the Whitney Independent Studio Program and has written essays that have been published by the New York Times.

b: Corinna Luyken is the author/illustrator of numerous picture books that have been translated into thirteen languages. These include The New York Times Best Seller, MY HEART; THE BOOK OF MISTAKES (A Bologna Children’s…
f: Corinna Luyken is the author/illustrator of numerous picture books that have been translated into thirteen languages. These include The New York Times Best Seller, MY HEART; THE BOOK OF MISTAKES (A Bologna Children’s Book Fair selection which The Wall Street Journal called “sublime”); ABC AND YOU AND ME (a Dolly Parton Imagination Library selection); THE TREE IN ME (an NCTE Notable Poetry Book and Indie Bestseller); THE ARGUERS (a School Library Best Picture Book of 2025) and most recently HELLO, OCEAN! She was raised in Oregon, California, and Hawaii; and studied dance improvisation, poetry, and printmaking at Middlebury College in Vermont. Her work is rooted in improvisation and explores themes of connection, perception, and misperception. She now lives near the Salish Sea where she likes to dig in the dirt, surf, and read with a cat (or two) on her lap.

b: Devika Cariapa trained as an archaeologist before finding her calling uncovering stories from stones, making the world of archaeology accessible for children. Her first book India through Archaeology: Excavating History…
f: Devika Cariapa trained as an archaeologist before finding her calling uncovering stories from stones, making the world of archaeology accessible for children. Her first book India through Archaeology: Excavating History received the Sahitya Akademi’s Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2019 and the Hindu Young World-Goodbooks Award 2018. Her subsequent works of non-fiction have been awarded the Neev Book Award, the Times of India AutHer Award and the Atta Galatta Bangalore Literature Festival Book Award. When she’s not writing, Devika dabbles in calligraphy and can most often be found wandering around ancient monuments or lingering with intent in one of Bangalore’s wonderful independent bookstores! b: Dipna Daryanani is a Mumbai-based movement artist, early years educator, author, and founder of Move with Joy, a creative movement program for young children. She is also the co-founder of Love the World Today, a…
f: Dipna Daryanani is a Mumbai-based movement artist, early years educator, author, and founder of Move with Joy, a creative movement program for young children. She is also the co-founder of Love the World Today, a sustainable children’s clothing brand. With over 18 years in early childhood education and more than a decade in contemporary dance and dance-theatre, Dipna’s work is rooted in curiosity, kindness, imagination, and embodied learning. As a performer, choreographer, educator, and movement coach, she creates experiences that invite presence, play, and connection. Her first children’s book, About the Friend in My Heart, explores kindness in the everyday. Across classrooms, studios, and stages, Dipna’s work seeks to nurture wonder, belonging, and authentic expression. Recent productions include The World can Wait, Not Same, Not Different, The Land of Mea Lilo and The Magical Garden, and, all reflecting her commitment to creating thoughtful, inclusive spaces where children and adults can connect more deeply with themselves, one another, and the world around them.

b: As a journalist, Harshikaa Udasi has chased news for most of her life, but what she enjoys the most is uncovering the story behind the news. Her stories for children largely dwell on the blurred lines between fact and…
f: As a journalist, Harshikaa Udasi has chased news for most of her life, but what she enjoys the most is uncovering the story behind the news. Her stories for children largely dwell on the blurred lines between fact and fiction. She has written the award-winning Kittu’s Very Mad Day (FICCI Children’s Book of the Year 2017), Friends Behind Walls (Parag Honor-list 2020), The Story Quilt, and the series Inspiring Tales from Indian History, among others. Her latest book is about the life and valour of Mewar’s Maharana Pratap. She has also contributed to several anthologies. Harshikaa runs Book Trotters Collaborative through which she creates rich reading spaces for schools, mentorship programmes for educators, and also a book club for children. Delegate | 2021 | 2026 Growing Boundaries: Relationships, Neighbourhoods & Questions | 2021

f: Himanjali’s children’s and YA books include The Stupendous Timetelling Superdog and Talking of Muskaan, which were shortlisted for the Crossword Book Award in 2013 and 2016, respectively, while her YA novel, The Lies We Tell, was shortlisted for The Neev Book Award in 2020. Forgetful Dida, a picture book by Himanjali, has been featured in the Parag Honour List 2025. b: Huthuka Sumi is a writer/photographer based in Dimapur, Nagaland. His debut GIANTS, a young adult novel set in Nagaland, won the 2025 AttaGalata BLF award in the children’s writing category. GIANTS has also currently…
f: Huthuka Sumi is a writer/photographer based in Dimapur, Nagaland. His debut GIANTS, a young adult novel set in Nagaland, won the 2025 AttaGalata BLF award in the children’s writing category. GIANTS has also currently been shortlisted for the Dehradun Literature Festival, Valley Of Words award for 2026. His focus areas are identity, voice, and the intersection of tribal expressions with mainstream spaces. He is currently working on his sophomore book. He and his wife share three overactive, boisterous boys.

b: Huw Aaron is a Welsh cartoonist, author and illustrator, and the creator of the bestselling picture book Sleep Tight, Disgusting Blob and middle-grade graphic novel Unfairies , both of which were shortlisted for the…
f: Huw Aaron is a Welsh cartoonist, author and illustrator, and the creator of the bestselling picture book Sleep Tight, Disgusting Blob and middle-grade graphic novel Unfairies , both of which were shortlisted for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize 2026—a historic achievement. After a short and fairly hopeless career in finance, Huw found a niche as a magazine cartoonist, producing joke cartoons for, among others, Private Eye, Prospect and The Spectator. Huw then started making comics and illustrating children’s books in his native Welsh. Since 2013, he has written or illustrated over 60 Welsh-language books, and has won numerous awards including the 2023 Tir na n-Og and Welsh Children’s Book of the Year prizes. He was also founding editor of the comic Mellten , and presented the weekly art programme Cer i Greu on S4C. His newest stories are Monkeypig and Unfairies: Death by Toad . Huw’s harshest critics—and his best friends—are his wife Luned and their two daughters.

b: Jayapriya Vasudevan is an agent and the founder of Jacaranda Literary Agency. Jacaranda was founded in India in 1997, and now runs out of Singapore with agents in Singapore, UK, and India. She currently lives in…
f: Jayapriya Vasudevan is an agent and the founder of Jacaranda Literary Agency. Jacaranda was founded in India in 1997, and now runs out of Singapore with agents in Singapore, UK, and India. She currently lives in Bangalore with her family. Her list focuses on gender and women writers, language, and inclusivity.

b: Kanishka Gupta is a well-known literary agent, writer, and publishing commentator based out of New Delhi. His agency, Writer’s Side, is acclaimed in the media to be a key player in South Asian publishing. His first…
f: Kanishka Gupta is a well-known literary agent, writer, and publishing commentator based out of New Delhi. His agency, Writer’s Side, is acclaimed in the media to be a key player in South Asian publishing. His first author Anees Salim has won India’s three most prestigious literary prizes: The Sahitya Akademi Award, The Crossword Book Award and The Hindu Literary Prize. His author Avni Doshi made it to the shortlist for the Booker Prize for Fiction 2020 for her debut novel Burnt Sugar/Girl in White Cotton. His agency has represented thousands of books, and has worked with several award winning authors and translators, including Banu Mushtaq and Deepa Bhasthi, winners of the 2025 International Booker for their collection of short stories, Heart Lamp, as well as Daisy Rockwell, translator for the 2022 International Booker winner, Tomb of Sand, Shehan Karunatilaka, winner of the 2022 Booker Prize, Avni Doshi, whose novel, Burnt Sugar, was shortlisted for the 2020 Booker prize, and Jerry Pinto, recipient of the 2016 Windham-Campbell prize. b: Kavita Singh Kale is an alumna of the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, and the University of Delhi, with a background in children’s content creation, animation filmmaking, and transmedia art practice. Known for…
f: Kavita Singh Kale is an alumna of the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, and the University of Delhi, with a background in children’s content creation, animation filmmaking, and transmedia art practice. Known for her vibrant and playful visual style, her multidisciplinary practice spans across installations, sculptures, book art, paintings, and films. When not writing, illustrating, or making art, she enjoys travelling. Inspired by people and everyday encounters, she creates character-driven narratives and intimate microcosm worlds drawn from close observation of life. Kavita is the co-founder of Underground Worm art and design studio, and currently serves as Associate Professor at Vidyashilp University. Delegate | 2025 | 2026

b: Kunaal has spent a little over two decades in sports content – eight of those years as a senior sports correspondent with the Times of India, and next 12 building the identity and content around sporting teams and…
f: Kunaal has spent a little over two decades in sports content – eight of those years as a senior sports correspondent with the Times of India, and next 12 building the identity and content around sporting teams and athletes at JSW Sports. He runs a small community on Instagram called Pitchside Recos that recommends books on sport, and later this year will be opening a little bookstore in the heart of Bengaluru.

b: Mala Kumar is an independent editor and writer who loves to engage with children of all ages through her writings, and through interactions in classrooms and bookish events. Her first book for middle-graders Up the…
f: Mala Kumar is an independent editor and writer who loves to engage with children of all ages through her writings, and through interactions in classrooms and bookish events. Her first book for middle-graders Up the Mountains of India was shortlisted for the Atta Galatta – Bangalore Literature Festival Children’s Non-fiction Award. In Travelling Treasures and Travelling Treasures 2.0, she presents the incredible tales behind everyday objects. In The Missing Rocks of Hampi she fuses history, mystery, water wisdom and present-day challenges. Her other books include Crazy Mazy’s Maths Puzzles, dozens of picture books and a biography of Sir M Visvesvaraya. Formerly an editor with the multi-lingual publisher Pratham Books, Mala enjoys talking to children, dogs, cats and plants.

b: Mamta Nainy is a writer based in New Delhi. She has authored over thirty-five books for children, many of which have gone on to win national and international awards and recognition, including Neev Book Award 2025,…
f: Mamta Nainy is a writer based in New Delhi. She has authored over thirty-five books for children, many of which have gone on to win national and international awards and recognition, including Neev Book Award 2025, Valley of Words Awards 2022, FICCI Publishing Awards 2022, Publishing Next Award 2022, The Hindu Young World-Goodbooks Award 2019 and Peek-a-Book Children’s Choice Award 2019. Her books have featured on the USBBY and IBBY lists. She also works as a literary translator, translating from Hindi into English, and vice versa. She is inspired by the unfettered imagination of children and loves travelling but is too lazy to do it, so she mostly makes do with reading. Delegate | 2019, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 Kashmir Stories | 2019

b: Mandira Shah is a part time writer and a full time software engineer, working and advocating for responsible AI. She is drawn to adventures far from the everyday — and writes the kind she’d love to get lost in herself,…
f: Mandira Shah is a part time writer and a full time software engineer, working and advocating for responsible AI. She is drawn to adventures far from the everyday — and writes the kind she’d love to get lost in herself, hoping you will too. Her debut novel Children of the Hidden Land won the Binod Kanoria Awards and the Valley of Words Award, and was shortlisted for the Auther Awards. Her second book, Muniya’s Quest, was shortlisted for the Binod Kanoria Award in middle-grade fiction. Her latest book “Off with their heads” is a sci-fi and grapples with the question if your thoughts are not your own, are you really you. She would love to hear from readers at mandira.shah@gmail.com

b: Mariyam Fatima is an author based in Delhi. She holds a Master’s degree in English Literature from Ambedkar University Delhi, where her research focused on Muslim women’s identity and resistance in literature. Her…
f: Mariyam Fatima is an author based in Delhi. She holds a Master’s degree in English Literature from Ambedkar University Delhi, where her research focused on Muslim women’s identity and resistance in literature. Her translations of poems by Sanjeev Kaushal have appeared in Indian Literature, the journal of Sahitya Akademi. She previously worked as a children’s editor at Penguin Random House India. Her books include Vincent Can’t Go, illustrated by Habib Ali, and My Name is Khadija, illustrated by Isha Nagar. Through her writing, Mariyam seeks to foster empathy, reflection and cultural understanding, creating stories that invite young readers to engage with diverse experiences and perspectives.

b: Meena Raghunathan has spent almost 40 years exploring how to design environmental and sustainability education which can make a difference, by engaging the heart, the head and the hands. She writes for…
f: Meena Raghunathan has spent almost 40 years exploring how to design environmental and sustainability education which can make a difference, by engaging the heart, the head and the hands. She writes for children–textbooks, fiction, stories etc., including the latest books on which this session is based ‘ALPHABET SOUP FOR THE YOUNG ENVIRONMENTALIST’ (Bookosmia). She also writes for professionals, educators and others. She loves to work with teachers and educators. She teaches courses for aspiring managers related to Responsible Business. She has worked in non-profits and the corporate world, and serves on corporate and NGO boards.

Previously, Namrata held editorial positions at HarperCollins, Disney-Hyperion, and Simon and Schuster. Namrata grew up in Afghanistan, India, Canada, Pakistan, Germany, and Poland. b: Nidhi Dhingra is a Bangalore-based independent creative, working at the intersection of art, culture and impact. With over 15 years of experience across publishing and narrative design, she brings a research-driven,…
f: Nidhi Dhingra is a Bangalore-based independent creative, working at the intersection of art, culture and impact. With over 15 years of experience across publishing and narrative design, she brings a research-driven, people-centric approach to storytelling through writing, illustration, and design. Previously, as Senior Editor at Goodearth Publications, Nidhi led over 30 print projects exploring the lesser-known cultural landscapes of India through travel guidebooks. Following this, she headed Content & Communications at INK Talks, shaping the voice of their multi-disciplinary conference and the INK Fellows Program. Driven by holistic impact and deep exploration, Nidhi collaborates with synergic organizations. Her client portfolio includes National Geographic, Royal Enfield, WWF India, Green Hub, Art1st Foundation, and RoundGlass Sustain.

b: Nina Sabnani is an animator, illustrator, researcher, and educator whose films weave together art, storytelling, ethnography, and oral traditions. Her collaborative works with artists and folk storytellers have received…
f: Nina Sabnani is an animator, illustrator, researcher, and educator whose films weave together art, storytelling, ethnography, and oral traditions. Her collaborative works with artists and folk storytellers have received national and international recognition. A graduate of the Faculty of Fine Arts, Vadodara, and a Fulbright Fellow with a master’s degree in film from Syracuse University, New York, her doctoral research on the Kaavad storytelling tradition led to the book Kaavad Tradition of Rajasthan: A Portable Pilgrimage. Sabnani co-founded the Animation Design programme at the National Institute of Design and later taught at IDC School of Design, IIT Bombay. She currently teaches at Srishti Manipal Institute of Art, Design and Technology, Bengaluru, and UPES, Dehradun, and serves as Festival Director of the AniMela International Animation Festival. Her honours include the National Award (Rajat Kamal) for Hum Chitra Banate Hain at the 64th National Film Awards (2016), the Big Little Book Award for Illustration (2018), the Legend of Indian Animation Award (2021), and the Ram Mohan Award of Excellence in Animation (2024).

b: Nirmal Kulkarni is a snake man and a story teller. His third line of conversation with a child or grown up is always about a fascinating nature incident or a snake adventure, every single time! As a conservation…
f: Nirmal Kulkarni is a snake man and a story teller. His third line of conversation with a child or grown up is always about a fascinating nature incident or a snake adventure, every single time! As a conservation scientist has been walking various forests for over 3 decades alongside forest communities, wildlife researchers and conservation scientists to conserve forests and their wild denizens. Nirmal has discovered 6 new species of amphibians from the Western Ghats of India and is Director of the Mhadei Research Centre, Goa. When not in field, Nirmal creates artworks from charcoal and recycled materials. He stays in Goa along with his photographer wife, an 11 year old bird watcher daughter and 2 dogs.

As a storyteller and children’s literature activist, she has been invited to address children, young adults and adults all over India and many parts of the world including Harvard University. Here, she spoke on Disruptive Innovation in children’s literature in India. She has worked with over 3 lakh children, especially those in difficult circumstances, using stories as a safe space to talk about hard things. She has received several awards including featuring on the IBBY Honor List and the Karubaki Award for fearless writing. f: Philippa Leathley grew up in East Yorkshire, spending summers near London with her eccentric grandparents and writing feverishly as soon as she could hold a pen. When not writing, she enjoys learning new languages, studying anything from historical fashion to shipwrecks, and is passionate about protecting the environment. She currently lives just outside Hull with her family and three weird and wonderful rescue cats, Bram, Lyra and Theo the Brave. Her debut novel, Inkbound: Meticulous Jones and the Skull Tattoo , was longlisted for the 2026 Branford Boase Award. The first book of her next children’s series, The Starsea Mysteries , will be published in 2028 following the conclusion of the Inkbound trilogy.

f: Before writing award-winning children’s books, Piers Torday worked as a producer in theatre and television, helping other people tell stories. His first children’s book, The Last Wild , was shortlisted for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize, with a stage adaptation due to premiere in 2027. Its sequel, The Dark Wild , won the 2014 Guardian Children’s Fiction Prize, and was followed by The Wild Beyond and The Wild Before . His other books include There May Be A Castle, The Lost Magician , The Frozen Sea , and Letters to a Dog. Midnight Treasure is the first part of a brand-new fantasy duology (with Wolf Crown ) about vampirs, werwolves, and treasure. Piers’ latest book is Tree Thing . He is also currently working on his next book, but he spends most of his time wrangling his very naughty but adorable dog, Huxley.

b: Pádraig Kenny is an Irish writer from County Kildare. He is a graduate of Maynooth University, where he obtained a master’s degree in Anglo-Irish writing. Previously an arts journalist, a teacher and a librarian’s…
f: Pádraig Kenny is an Irish writer from County Kildare. He is a graduate of Maynooth University, where he obtained a master’s degree in Anglo-Irish writing. Previously an arts journalist, a teacher and a librarian’s assistant, he now writes full-time. Pádraig’s debut, Tin , was a Waterstones Book of the Month and was nominated for the Carnegies, as well as being shortlisted for the Irish Book Award and several regional awards. His other acclaimed books include Pog, The Monsters of Rookhaven, and The Shadows of Rookhaven . b: Rahil Mohsin is a Bangalore-based comic artist, writer, and co-founder of Hallubol, the world’s first bilingual Dakhni-English comic series. With over 15 years of experience in comics and illustration, he has worked…
f: Rahil Mohsin is a Bangalore-based comic artist, writer, and co-founder of Hallubol, the world’s first bilingual Dakhni-English comic series. With over 15 years of experience in comics and illustration, he has worked with publishers including Scout Comics, Scholastic, Pratham Books, Room to Read, and contributed to the anthology Comixense. Alongside self-publishing his own comics, he has illustrated several children’s books, while Fayu & Dariya Ka Jinn marks his debut as both writer and illustrator. His work explores Dakhni language, folklore, neighbourhood culture, food, and the everyday lives of South Indian Muslim communities through comics and picture books. Across his practice, Rahil is interested in preserving oral traditions, multilingual storytelling, and overlooked cultural histories through visual narratives.

f: Richa Jha is a picture book author and the founder and publisher of Pickle Yolk Books, an independent children’s publishing house. Picture books written by her delve into the internal world of children and adults as they explore the many ways in which the mind thinks, stoops, rejects, questions, plays tricks, recovers, sings, flies and empowers. Her works have been translated into several languages, including Hindi, Malayalam, Bangla, Kannada and Marathi in India, and in French, Polish, Russian and Thai. Most of her titles have won national and international recognition across platforms. A passionate advocate of picture books being a wholesome read for all ages, she believes that there is no better life coach than a picture book created just right. f: Samhita Arni has been passionate about retelling mythology in contemporary cultural contexts since childhood. She has authored four books, beginning at age 11 with The Mahabharata — A Child’s View, published in over seven languages and selling over 60,000 copies. Her second book, Sita’s Ramayana, a collaboration with artist Moyna Chitrakar, became a New York Times Bestseller. The Missing Queen is a spec-fi mythological thriller based on the Ramayana, and The Prince, a historical fiction set in the Sangam era, won the 2020 Neev Book Award. As an adult, Samhita explores the critical ways women participate in and are excluded from mythological and historical narratives. She also an educator and is retraining as a psychologist, aiming to reimagine stories that shape more liberating identities for ourselves and our children. f: Samina Mishra is a documentary filmmaker, writer, and teacher based in New Delhi. Her work uses the lens of childhood, identity and education to reflect the experiences of growing up in India. Her recent work includes the books The Night Sky, Lines and Roop and the River Crossing, The Hum Hindustani Poetry Podcast on children and citizenship, and The Incredible Child, an arts-based programme for Afghan refugee children at the Simurgh Centre, Delhi. Samina founded The Magic Key Centre for the Arts and Childhood that works on intersections between childhood, the arts and education. Samina hopes that her work makes children think about the world they want to live in, and encourages adults to support children in realising that world.

Samira serves on the national board of Authors Against Book Bans. And when she’s not writing, reading, or fighting censorship, you can find her on her quest for the perfect pastry. When she isn’t making books, she can usually be found drinking tea, buying more books than she can read, writing the occasional poem, or pursuing her ambition to become a full-time houseplant. As a journalist covering deep tech, AI, and science for Hindustan Times, she brings the excitement of real discovery into her storytelling. Find her at @shwetawrites.

Her authored books include Guardians of Gobuk, The Monster Who Could Not Climb a Tree and Something to Chew On, among others. Alongside writing, Tanya has worked for over a decade in community-led conservation, supporting Indigenous Peoples’ and local community initiatives. Her work has included programme strategy, documentation, environmental education and the development of the Community Conserved Areas (CCA) portal, which documents grassroots conservation efforts from across the country. She has also created educational resources and reading programmes for children. She enjoys wildlife watching, travel, music, books, gardening and swimming. Delegate | 2023, 2026

b: Tara Gandhi is a nature conservationist who was guided by Dr Sálim Ali for her M.Sc in Zoology with specialisation in Field Ornithology. She worked for biodiversity conservation with many organisations in India and…
f: Tara Gandhi is a nature conservationist who was guided by Dr Sálim Ali for her M.Sc in Zoology with specialisation in Field Ornithology. She worked for biodiversity conservation with many organisations in India and abroad and has conducted status studies of Indian wildlife protected areas including in remote islands of Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep. She enjoys documenting wildlife near her home and wherever travels. Currently, Tara Gandhi is Vice-Chair of the Wildlife Trust of India and serves on the committees of BNHS-India, Madras Naturalists’ Society and the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT-M). The author of books on ecology, scientific and popular articles, Tara is the editor of anthologies of Dr.Sálim Ali’s writings and his radio talks.

Over the last 15 years she has published over 350 stories in print and digital media. She loves writing about untold histories, unexplored places, unsung people, and unheard nonhumans. Shroff has received many national and international awards for her work, including The Times of India AutHer Award 2023, and has been part of prestigious lists including The White Ravens International List 2023, and the Parag Honour List 2025. Her recent works include ‘Submerged Worlds and Other Amazing Stories of India’s Mighty Rivers’, ‘10 Indian Scientists Whose Extraordinary Work You May Not Know’, ‘Ganesh Pyne’s Twilight Dreams’ and ‘Viv and Panther Land on Mars’. She has also written the script for the first ever short film on Indian dinosaurs, ‘Rajasaur – The Movie’, produced and directed by an LA-based filmmaker. She prefers children over adults, chai over coffee and chocolate over everything else. Delegate | 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026
